title: Germs in a stalk are represented and compared on members of a basis
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology, $\mathcal P$ a presheaf of abelian groups (or of sets, rings, modules) on $X$ and $x\in X$, with stalk $\mathcal P_x$ and germs $s\mapsto s_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then (i) every element of $\mathcal P_x$ is the germ $s_x$ of some $s\in\mathcal P(U)$ with $U\in\mathcal B$, $x\in U$; (ii) for open $U,V\ni x$, $s\in\mathcal P(U)$, $t\in\mathcal P(V)$ with $s_x=t_x$ there is $W\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in W\subseteq U\cap V$ and $s|_W=t|_W$.

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Section 009H, remark after Definition 009I (the stalk may be computed over the members of B containing x, since they form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of x) and the remark after Lemma 009N (F_x = F^ext_x)
